mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly FEDFUNDS rate above the prior month's level, followed by a sustained 30-day hold, predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate tighter policy and reduced risk appetite.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its previous month's value and remains elevated for two consecutive months
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in at least 70% of similar FEDFUNDS spikes, or the 20-day return is statistically indistinguishable from the prior month's return (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls by more than 0.25 percentage points from its prior 3-month average, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be positive as expectations of future easing support equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: 3-month MA of FEDFUNDS drops > 0.25 pp from the previous 3-month MA
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 50% of such FEDFUNDS declines, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) after controlling for lagged SPX returns.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment months) exceeding 10,000 above the prior month's level, accompanied by a simultaneous decline in UNRATE by at least 0.1 percentage points, predicts a positive S&P 20-day forward return as labor market strength offsets inflationary pressures.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > PAYEMS previous month + 10,000 AND UNRATE < UNRATE previous month + 0.1 pp
regime_hint: labor market strengthening with cooling inflation expectations
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of such labor strength/inflation weakening events, or the interaction coefficient in a regression is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly rise in HOUST (residential building permits) of at least 5% followed by a 2-month plateau predicts a positive S&P 5-day forward return as a signal of growing construction activity and economic momentum.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by > 5% in month t and remains flat in month t+1
regime_hint: early stage of a housing recovery
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative in > 60% of such permit spikes, or the effect is not robust across multiple economic shocks (e.g., oil price spikes).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in INDPRO (industrial production index) of at least 2% followed by a 3-month stabilization predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as weak manufacturing output suggests contractionary pressures that weigh on equities.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 2% in month t and remains below prior month's value for three consecutive months
regime_hint: early signs of a soft landing turning into contraction
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in > 50% of such INDPRO contractions, or the effect is not significant after controlling for macroeconomic risk factors.

mechanism_narrative: When the 4-week moving average of GDPC1 (real private consumption) exceeds expectations by at least 2% and FEDFUNDS remains below 1.00%, the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to be positive as excess demand supports valuation expansion.
candidate_trigger: 4-week MA GDPC1 > prior 4-week MA + 2% AND FEDFUNDS < 1.00%
regime_hint: over-optimistic consumption growth with policy easing
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are negative in > 40% of such events, or the interaction term is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in UNRATE below 5% for three consecutive months in a labor market expansion regime predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as rising labor costs erode profit margins and equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 5% for three consecutive months AND UNRATE trend is downward
regime_hint: labor market expansion with rising wage pressures
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in > 60% of such UNRATE declines, or the effect is not robust to oil price shocks.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous drop in both INDPRO and RSAFS (retail sales) by at least 3% in the same month, followed by a 10-day hold, predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return as weak demand and weak production jointly depress growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by > 3% AND RSAFS falls by > 3% in month t and both remain flat for the next 10 trading days
regime_hint: dual softening in manufacturing and retail demand
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are non-negative in > 50% of such dual softening events, or the interaction coefficient is not significant (p > 0.10).
